In [[topology]], a branch of mathematics, an '''excisive triad''' is a triple <math>(X; A, B)</math> of [[topological space]]s such that ''A'', ''B'' are subspaces of ''X'' and ''X'' is the union of the interior of ''A'' and the interior of ''B''.<ref>{{harvnb|May|2019|loc=Ch 10. Section 7.}}</ref> Note ''B'' is not required to be a [[Subspace topology|subspace]] of ''A''.
